summary: A tower erected in 1930 in Morgan-Monroe State Forest, condemned and rebuilt by youth crews in 2009-2010, renovated again by 2026; the gate is often locked.

facts.design: Three-section steel tower with a cab; cabin floor and ceiling replaced with white oak in the 2009-2010 rebuild

access.note: Mark A says the gate around the tower is locked most of the time. A June 2026 tornado made parts of the forest inaccessible, per Mark A.

visit.trail_note: Visit Bloomington says Trail 5 leads to the tower from inside Morgan-Monroe State Forest. Check current access first, because the gate is usually locked.

events.note: Sign at the tower and the NHLR give 1930. Mark A quotes a survey note that says sources are confusing, and a 1931 state report mentions an eighty-foot steel tower.
Condemned before the work. Young Hoosiers Conservation Corp (YHCC) crews rebuilt it over two seasons, 2009 and 2010.
Dennis Goen was a Mason Ridge towerman from 1963 to 1965, per an interview from a 2013 IDNR video that Mark A cites.
Visit Bloomington's April 2026 guide calls the tower newly renovated and available again after being closed for a year. The post gives no dates for the closure.
Registered July 21, 2026 as US 1832, IN 13; nominated by Jason Johns.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief and NHLR place the tower in Morgan County, Indiana. Mark A lists it under Monroe County and says two Mason Ridge sites are listed online. The record keeps Morgan County because the NHLR is the register of record, but an editor should confirm.

The 1930 date from the tower sign, the NHLR and the 1930 notice conflicts with a 1931 state report that mentions an eighty-foot tower and a survey note saying the sources are confusing. The story reports both.
Mark A gives June 17, 2026 in one place and June 16, 2026 in a heading. The story says mid-June.

notes_for_editor: The brief's agency 'State Forest' is not an agency, and none of the readable sources names the agency that administers this tower, so the agency fact is left out. The access level 'restricted' rests on Mark A's note that the gate is usually locked; the Visit Bloomington post says the tower is available again. The 2026 'restored' event is dated only by the April 2026 post, so its year may not match the renovation. No Living New Deal or Facebook sources were checked for this tower.
